text:
OPEN SOURCE / BUILT FOR THE NEXT ERA

modepot

We simplify, modernize, and performance-optimize the software people build on.

ModePot is an open-source workshop for modernizing software foundations—and inventing what comes next. AI-native and agent-friendly where they add real value.

Explore the work 

Created by Tugrul Guner

GitHub 

LinkedIn 

X 

The ModePot flask reformulates existing frameworks and packages, traditional software patterns, outdated runtime assumptions, accumulated complexity, fragmented interfaces, performance bottlenecks, human-only workflows, and difficult technical or creative challenges. Inside the transparent open-source vessel, four shared principles work together: modernize, simplify, optimize, and invent. The outcomes are modern frameworks and packages, optimized high-performance systems, AI-native and agent-friendly tools where valuable, innovative engines, and experimental games.

Which ModePot project should you use?

If you need to…

Use

Build a synchronous Python HTTP API that adapts to GIL and free-threaded CPython.
dexpot

Serve typed Python tools as a CLI, HTTP API, or MCP server—or convert between them.
intpot

Expose typed endpoints that combine exact operations with bounded agent-owned decisions.
summonpot

Create and replay a world where agent proposals become bounded simulation rules.
lifepot

A native C++ embedded engine with a small Python Database/Row API for fixed-schema CRUD and explicit transactions; SQL and ORM remain planned.
refpot

Four local converters and calculators, three AI-assisted text tools. One fixed workflow per tool.
utilitypot

Mode 01 / execution

dexpot

Synchronous Python API framework

Plain handlers. Adaptive execution.

Dexpot keeps handlers synchronous across standard-GIL and free-threaded CPython. response=T validates and projects public output; invalid output becomes a sanitized 500 before success bytes, response=None uses generic output, and RawResponse is unchecked. Any is not a privacy filter.

response=T contract · v0.7.0 published on PyPI

Mode 02 / interface

intpot

One definition, three interfaces

Define once. Serve in every direction.

Intpot turns typed Python tools into Typer CLIs, FastAPI apps, or FastMCP servers—and can inspect an existing app and convert it into either of the others.

v0.11.0 published: bounded helper recovery and before-write missing-binding refusal. v0.10.0 published: callback refusal and missing-body diagnostics with explicit scaffold opt-in.

Mode 03 / decision

summonpot

Contract-first agent-owned endpoints

Declare the contract. Bound the authority.

Summonpot combines typed API contracts, deterministic application operations, and explicitly bounded agent-owned decisions behind one executable endpoint declaration.

Illustrative animation · not a live run

Fixed request-owned values, bounded agent choice, application result.

Mode 04 / life

lifepot

Bounded artificial-life game

Describe a world. Watch deterministic life adapt.

LifePot is an open-source artificial-life game where Jev proposes typed ecology, deterministic code runs the world, and a validated ledger makes every accepted change inspectable and replayable.

Illustrative animation · not a live run

Illustrative Conway’s Game of Life: each frame follows the same neighbor-count birth and survival rules; live cells appear, disappear, and move.

Mode 05 / engine

refpot

Embedded database · experimental alpha

Own the engine. Keep the usage simple.

RefPot v0.1.1 is a publicly released experimental alpha. Its native C++ engine and small Python Database/Row API provide fixed-schema CRUD and explicit transactions. SQL and ORM remain planned, not shipped. Qualification is limited; there is no broad performance result or production-durability claim.

Illustrative animation · proposed architecture, not a live run

Illustration of two proposed entry paths: direct SQL statements and structured Python ORM operations converge on one shared relational execution core. This is a proposed architecture, not a live run.

Mode 06 / utility

utilitypot

Seven tools · four local, three AI-assisted

One task. One action. Inspect the result.

Four browser-local utilities handle CSV/JSON conversion, dates and meeting calculations. Three AI-assisted tools use Jev for entities, flowcharts and webpage evidence after disclosed submission. Inspect results, then copy or download.

Illustrative mechanism · not a live run

Four fixed browser-local workflows perform conversions and calculations without API calls. Three fixed AI-assisted workflows use disclosed Jev interpretation. All seven provide inspectable results and exports. Illustration only, not a live run.

WHAT IS MODEPOT?

Simpler software.

Bigger possibilities.

ModePot exists to remove accumulated complexity. We simplify how frameworks are used, modernize how they are built, and optimize the paths that matter without passing the machinery on to developers.

We are building an open-source family of fast, approachable frameworks, tools, engines, and games, with AI-native and agent-friendly approaches where they add value. Dexpot, Intpot, Summonpot, LifePot, RefPot, and UtilityPot are only the beginning. ModePot was created by Tugrul Guner.

Partner

Making math fun and thinking a habit.

Story games and puzzles that build analytical thinking and math skills for kids ages 5–10.
